title: Impact of Comments on LLM Comprehension of Legacy Code
review_status: full-text audit complete; one-module study design, four tested model families, SME-created quizzes, comment-density/accuracy outcomes, training-exposure signal, and author-stated MCQ limitations checked
sections_checked: Research questions and experimental design
L8WAIT code variants and SME quiz construction
Four-model evaluation and three-run procedure
Results for comment density, 20% inaccurate comments, and completely inaccurate comments
Conclusion and future work: one module, option-position bias and generalization limits
venue_year_verified: arXiv:2506.11007v1, submitted 2025-04-23; paper labels results preliminary; no peer-reviewed venue identified in reviewed version
evidence_note: Four LLMs on one IBM z/OS assembler module; increased comments often raised custom MCQ scores. Twenty percent inaccurate comments had negligible effect for most models; wholly inaccurate comments reduced the average advanced-question score from 73% to 61%. No-code quiz score averaged 75%, a possible training exposure signal. Three repeats; answer-option position not randomized per future-work section.

venue_year_verified: arXiv:2511.07463v1, submitted 2025-11-07; no peer-reviewed venue identified in reviewed version
evidence_note: The study evaluates 11 LLMs on BigO(Bench) (311 problems) and CodeContests. It reports structural/runtime trace variation even among solutions passing public tests and a tendency for higher temperature to increase pass@1 and instability in its temperature sweep. Each configuration uses five samples; authors explicitly restrict external validity because of Python-only execution and test-suite dependence; proposed metrics are not shown to predict production incidents.

venue_year_verified: arXiv:2606.08676v1, submitted 2026-06-07; no peer-reviewed venue identified in reviewed version
evidence_note: Across Qwen2.5-Coder and DeepSeek-Coder, instruction tuning often harms FIM but improves some guidance-heavy completion tasks; magnitude and significance depend on model family and benchmark. Checkpoint effects are non-monotonic. Authors note only two model families, undisclosed corpora/possible contamination, controlled small-scale tuning, offline function-level tasks and no developer study.

title: Testing the Effect of Code Documentation on Large Language Model Code Understanding
review_status: targeted full-text follow-up inspected via ACL primary PDF; HumanEval unit-test proxy, support for harmful incorrect docs, null correctness effect for correct comments, coverage difference, contamination/generalization limitations checked; same two authors as one batch63 sample, not independent replication
sections_checked: Sections 3-5: code-understanding proxy, 164 HumanEval functions, GPT-3.5/GPT-4 outputs, comment variants and bootstrap comparisons
Section 6: null effect on test-success rate but higher coverage with comments; wrong comments significantly harmful
Section 7: single benchmark and possible training contamination limitations
venue_year_verified: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2024, pages 1044-1050
evidence_note: Comments did not significantly improve successful unit-test rate over no comments, but increased line coverage; random unrelated comments significantly reduced test success and coverage. Both authors overlap with the 2025 legacy-assembler study, so this is same-group evidence rather than independent replication. The study uses GPT-3.5/GPT-4 and HumanEval only.

title: Extending Fill-In-the-Middle with Instructions for Steerable Code Completion
review_status: targeted arXiv full-text HTML follow-up inspected; IFIM objective, synthetic instruction corpus, two-model-family results, 100-real-developer-instruction test, and local-context limitations checked
sections_checked: Sections 3-4: structurally separated instruction objective, 122.9k synthesized examples and benchmark construction
Section 5 tables: instruction/no-instruction results for two backbones and Qwen model-size checks
In-the-wild test: 100 post-training-cutoff developer TODO/FIXME examples
Conclusion and limitations: long-context/repository generalization remains untested
venue_year_verified: arXiv:2509.24637v3, revised 2026-09-03; full text available from arXiv HTML
evidence_note: A task-specific IFIM objective improves instruction-conditioned FIM scores on two code model families while usually preserving no-instruction capability; one Qwen IFIM ordering regresses without instructions. A 100-example developer-authored TODO/FIXME evaluation favors IFIM. Training instructions are GPT-4.1-synthesized, benchmark instructions are also synthesized then manually revised, only two families are tested, and RepoMaster context is truncated to 20 prefix/suffix lines; this counters inevitability of a tuning tradeoff but does not settle long-context performance.
